clue.text: Feel best fitted, though the least competent

indicators.note: the letters are fitted together again in a new order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says they feel at their best in a suit, despite being the least able of the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitted' sounds like tailoring but tells you to rearrange FEEL BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble means weak or ineffective, so the superlative describes whoever is least capable.

clue.text: Following decline, a European is for raising the standard

indicators.note: following places the second piece after the first, so the European comes after the word for decline

parts.note: to flag is to weaken or decline
a Pole is a person from Poland

explanation.surface: After a slump, a European figure is the one to restore high standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' is a flag, not a level of quality; 'Following' puts POLE after FLAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall mast is the post on which a banner or standard is hoisted.

clue.text: Wrote in large letters "Occupied"

definitions.meaning: to engross a document is to write it out in large formal script

explanation.definitionFit: A legal clerk who copies a deed in big formal handwriting does this, and a person wholly absorbed in a task is equally described.

clue.text: The sailor naturally embraces a woman

indicators.note: the phrase embraces the woman's name, which sits inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A seaman, as is only natural, gives a woman a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' tells you the name is held within 'sailor naturally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorna is a female given name, as in Lorna Doone.

clue.text: It's splendid beneath a tree!

parts.note: sub- is the prefix meaning under or beneath
the lime or linden is a tree

explanation.surface: Someone lying under a tree declares the spot glorious.
explanation.definitionFit: Sublime means awe-inspiringly excellent or grand.

clue.text: Lay around sick in lodgings

indicators.note: around shows the wager word wrapping round the word for sick

parts.note: to lay money is to bet
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone lies about feeling unwell in their rented rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' reads as reclined, but here it is a wager; 'around' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet is a soldier's quarters, accommodation in a private house.

clue.text: The gelatine is in a transparent container

parts.note: a glass is a see-through vessel for drinks

explanation.surface: Some gelatine is sitting in a clear jar.
explanation.definitionFit: Isinglass is a pure form of gelatine obtained from fish bladders.

clue.text: Turner's left with two articles

definitions.note: read as 'Turner is', the definition being a turner

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: The painter Turner has gone, leaving a couple of pieces behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter; here it is anything that turns wood or metal, and the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine that rotates a workpiece so it can be shaped, a tool for turning.

clue.text: Setting the pitch to rights

parts.note: sounds like groundsmen repairing a sports field, but it is about adjusting a musical note so it is true

explanation.definitionFit: Adjusting an instrument so its notes sound at the correct frequency is this process.

clue.text: A good-looker, a big shot in the underworld, holding on

indicators.note: holding means the name of the underworld god wraps around the word on

parts.note: Dis is the Roman ruler of the underworld, also the name of his realm

explanation.surface: A handsome man is a gangland boss clinging on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big shot in the underworld' suggests a Mafia don, but it is DIS, the god of the dead, who holds ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis, the youth loved by Venus, stands for any strikingly handsome young man.

clue.text: Sound forecaster doing a boring job

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a tool rather than a noun

indicators.note: sound signals that the answer is a word pronounced like the forecaster word

parts.note: an augur was a Roman soothsayer who predicted the future

explanation.surface: A reliable weatherman has a dull assignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable; it signals a homophone. 'boring' means drilling holes.
explanation.definitionFit: An auger is a drilling tool for making holes in wood or soil.

clue.text: Drink from poor quality china

parts.note: bad means of poor quality
Minton is a famous English make of porcelain

explanation.surface: Someone sips from a cheap, inferior cup.
explanation.walkthrough: Badminton here is not the sport but a claret cup, a wine punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is an old name for a cold cup of claret, soda and sugar.

clue.text: In favour of people turning hands down

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Supporters of the populace refuse to give anything a thumbs up.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronation is the rotation of the forearm so the palm faces downward.

clue.text: Historian aware of environmental responsibility

definitions.meaning: J. R. ... wrote A Short History of the English People

explanation.definitionFit: John Richard Green was a Victorian historian, and the colour word also labels eco-friendly politics.

clue.text: The inexperienced driver is not entirely flexible

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car
some means a part but not the whole

explanation.surface: A learner motorist is only partly adaptable.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L plate, so L stands for an inexperienced driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissome means supple and lithe in body.

clue.text: Didn't budget carefully, so even sport might be affected

indicators.note: affected means changed, so the letters of the two words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spent too freely, so even their sporting hobby might suffer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be affected' rearranges EVEN SPORT; 'so' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending more than the money allowed is a failure to stick to a budget.

clue.text: Cast about and find the drink

indicators.note: about shows the throwing word placed round the word and

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast

explanation.surface: Someone searches around to locate their drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast about' looks like one phrase for searching, but 'Cast' means throw and 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is beer mixed with lemonade.

clue.text: One may well see his work as play

definitions.text: One may well see his work as play

parts.words: One may well see his work as play
parts.note: seems to describe someone who finds labour fun, but his output is literally a stage piece

explanation.definitionFit: A playwright writes pieces for the theatre, so what he produces is drama.

clue.text: This individual's barely prepared to move in a hurry

definitions.text: This individual's barely prepared to move in a hurry

parts.words: This individual's barely prepared to move in a hurry
parts.note: seems to be a person scarcely ready to rush, but barely means naked: someone who dashes in the nude

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs naked through a public place, often a sports ground, for a prank.

clue.text: A commercial outlet is coming

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement or commercial
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: An advertised shop is about to open.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means an arrival, the coming of something important.

clue.text: Give up and go to bed

definitions.meaning: to hand over or surrender, as to the police

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both handing something over to authorities and retiring for the night.

clue.text: Pressing takes only a moment

definitions.meaning: a very brief point of time

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both urgent and a split second.

clue.text: Sent in agitated note, being very emotional

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters of the two words are shaken into a new order

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone sent an anxious message, being highly emotional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' turns SENT IN into INTENS, and the note E completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense describes feelings that are strong and deeply felt.

clue.text: The way to put a chap right about certain points

indicators.note: about shows the man-and-right pair surrounding the compass letters

parts.note: man means a chap
N and E are compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: This is how you correct a fellow regarding a few details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right about' looks like 'correct about', but 'about' signals that the chap and R wrap round two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Manner means the way something is done.

clue.text: Gather for a service in church

parts.note: Mass is the Eucharist service in Catholic churches

explanation.surface: People assemble for worship.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate.

clue.text: Thirty days may be quietly accepted by crooked liar

indicators.note: accepted by means the soft letter is taken inside the jumbled word
crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters of liar are rearranged

parts.note: p (piano) means quietly in music

explanation.surface: A thirty-day sentence might be silently accepted by a dishonest fibber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges LIAR to ARIL; 'accepted by' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: April is one of the months with thirty days, as the rhyme says.

clue.text: Explanation given by odious creature — one on the beer

parts.note: a rat is a despised animal or person
I is the Roman numeral for one
ale is beer

explanation.surface: An excuse offered by a despicable drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning or justification behind something.

clue.text: Striking serving men is not the done thing

parts.note: workers out are on strike
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Soldiers going on strike would be quite improper.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, men serving in the British army.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means unconventional and beyond accepted propriety.

clue.text: Wearing no make-up is foreign

indicators.note: make-up is taken as the way something is made up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Going without cosmetics is an alien custom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like cosmetics but signals rearranging WEARING NO.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norwegian, from Norway, is foreign from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Concentrated, being dense

definitions.meaning: of liquid, heavy and not runny

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes soup that is heavy and undiluted and a person who is slow to understand.

clue.text: Tell of a minister losing his head

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, of the church dignitary word is removed

parts.note: a prelate is a high-ranking churchman

explanation.surface: Report on a clergyman being decapitated.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate is to narrate or recount.

clue.text: Person showing a preference for the French or Spanish in part

definitions.text: Person showing a preference for the French or Spanish in part

parts.words: Person showing a preference for the French or Spanish in part
parts.note: someone who picks, choosing between rivals; the word itself also holds both the French and Spanish for the within it

explanation.surface: Someone favours the French or the Spanish to some degree.
explanation.walkthrough: A selector chooses; its letters also contain LE (French 'the') and EL (Spanish 'the') in part.
explanation.definitionFit: One who chooses, such as someone who picks a team, shows a preference.
